- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for next 7–14 days.  
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising forecasts) with low sentiment, reduce slope; mean-revert to 1–2 prior-day average.  
- If model shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive falling forecasts) with high sentiment, reduce downward bias; add 0.5–1.5% upward correction.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 7–10 days if sentiment is neutral or mixed.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.00, -0.50, 0.67), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% lag correction to forecast for next 3–5 days.
